Compare the logistic calibration with flexible curves

Source: R/calibration_curves.R
compare_calibration_curves.Rd

Checks the shape of the calibration curve before a threshold is taken from it. For each group (by default, each species), fits the probability that a reviewed clip is a true positive as a function of the logit of its score with four curves: the logistic of fit_calibration() (linear in the logit), a quadratic, a GAM (mgcv) and a monotone increasing GAM (scam). Each curve is judged where the threshold lies, not on average, and its thresholds are compared with the model-free threshold of the weighted precision (suggest_thresholds()).

Usage

compare_calibration_curves(
  validation,
  target = 0.95,
  by = "species_folder",
  curves = c("logistic", "quadratic", "gam", "monotone_gam"),
  weighted = NULL,
  k = 5,
  k_folds = 5,
  cv = TRUE,
  cluster = "source_audio",
  top_from = 0.7,
  bin_width = 0.05,
  min_n = 15,
  min_bin = 5,
  max_error = 0.03,
  tolerance = 0.03,
  grid_step = 0.01,
  seed = 2026
)

Arguments

validation

Reviewed clips, as for suggest_thresholds(): with verdict ("positive" or "negative"; others are left out), confidence and, for weights, inclusion_prob.

target

Target probability (threshold_p_tp) and precision (threshold_precision, threshold_weighted). Several targets can be given: the curves and the cross-validation are fitted once per group, and the result has one row per group x target x curve.

by

Columns of validation that define the groups fitted separately. "species_folder" by default; c("site", "species_folder") fits each cell.

curves

Curves to fit, among "logistic", "quadratic", "gam" and "monotone_gam". "gam" needs the package mgcv and "monotone_gam" the package scam; a curve whose package is missing is left out with a message.

weighted

NULL (weight by 1 / inclusion_prob the groups whose clips all have it), TRUE or FALSE.

k

Basis dimension of the GAMs (reduced when the group has fewer distinct scores).

k_folds

Number of folds of the cross-validation.

cv

FALSE skips the cross-validation (cv_logloss, cv_logloss_se and within_1se are NA), when only the thresholds and the verdict, which does not use it, are needed.

cluster

Column of validation whose levels are kept together in the folds ("source_audio", the recording, by default). Without it, clips are split one by one.

top_from, bin_width

Lower limit and width of the high score bins of top_error.

min_n

Minimum number of clips of a group, of (effective) clips at or above a cut for it to count, and of effective clips in the high bins.

min_bin

Minimum number of clips of a bin for it to enter top_error.

max_error, tolerance

Largest top_error_excess and largest difference between the logistic and the weighted thresholds, in score units, for "keep_logistic".

grid_step

Step of the grid of scores of threshold_p_tp and of the curves returned.

seed

Seed of the folds. The global random number generator is left as it was.

Value

A tibble with one row per group x target x curve: the by columns, curve, target, n, n_positive, cv_logloss, cv_logloss_se, within_1se (log-loss within one standard error of the best curve of the group), top_error, top_error_excess, n_eff_top, max_p, reaches_target, threshold_p_tp, threshold_precision, threshold_weighted, diff_weighted, above_reviewed (a threshold above the highest reviewed score is an extrapolation), weighted and verdict. The attribute "curves" holds the fitted curves on the grid (score, p_tp) and "bins" the observed precision by bin, for plot_calibration_curves().

Details

What is compared. For each curve:

  • cv_logloss: log-loss of held-out clips in k_folds-fold cross-validation, with folds made of whole recordings (cluster), so that clips of the same recording are not split between fitting and testing. It is dominated by the bulk of the clips, mostly at low scores, and may tie across curves even when one is wrong near the threshold; use it together with top_error.

  • top_error: calibration error in the high score bins (width bin_width, from top_from to 1): the mean, weighted by the effective number of clips of each bin, of the absolute difference between the observed precision of the bin and the mean probability predicted by the curve for its clips. Part of it is the sampling noise of the bins, shared by every curve, so top_error_excess (the error of the curve minus the smallest error of the flexible curves) is what the verdict uses.

  • threshold_p_tp: the lowest score from which the curve stays at or above target (the rule "probability" of calibrated_thresholds()), on a grid of step grid_step. max_p is the highest value of the curve within the reviewed scores; when it stays below target, no score guarantees the target (reaches_target = FALSE).

  • threshold_precision: the lowest score from which the precision of the clips kept, as predicted by the curve (the mean of the predicted probabilities of the reviewed clips at or above the cut, weighted by 1 / inclusion_prob), stays at or above target. It answers the same question as the weighted count, threshold_weighted, so diff_weighted (their difference) is direct evidence on the shape of the curve.

Verdict. One per group, following the decision table of the threshold workflow:

  • "too_few_clips": fewer than min_n clips, or fewer than two of either verdict; no curve is fitted.

  • "sample_more_near_threshold": fewer than min_n effective clips in the high score bins; a new round there (sampling_mode = "score_bands" in select_clips(), joined by combine_rounds()) is needed before deciding.

  • "no_curve_reaches_target": neither the flexible curves nor the weighted count give a threshold with precision target (with at least min_n effective clips above it). The curve levels off before the target, or reaches it only at the very top, and no usable score guarantees it: improve the classifier before setting a threshold.

  • "keep_logistic": the logistic has top_error_excess <= max_error and its threshold_precision is within tolerance of the weighted count. A flexible curve may still fit better in log-loss, but away from the threshold.

  • "use_monotone_or_weighted": larger error in the high bins, or thresholds that disagree; take the threshold from the monotone GAM or from the weighted precision (suggest_thresholds(), threshold_bootstrap()).

Which clips. Clips of any probability design can be used: "random_detections" and "score_bands" clips carry inclusion_prob, and are weighted by 1 / inclusion_prob in the fits and in the precision (weighted = NULL does so when every clip of the group has it). Clips of "top" have no inclusion probability; with them, the weighted count is not an estimate of the precision of the predictions. Fitting with and without weights (weighted = TRUE and FALSE) is also a check of the shape: similar thresholds mean the shape is right.

References

Wood, C. M. & Kahl, S. (2024). Guidelines for appropriate use of BirdNET scores and other detector outputs. Journal of Ornithology, 165, 777-782. doi:10.1007/s10336-024-02144-5

See also

fit_calibration(), compare_calibration_models(), calibrated_thresholds(), suggest_thresholds(), threshold_bootstrap().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
cmp <- compare_calibration_curves(validation, target = 0.95)
cmp[c("species_folder", "curve", "top_error", "threshold_precision",
      "threshold_weighted", "verdict")]
plot_calibration_curves(cmp)
} # }
